# A large convex subbody repairs the four-dimensional selector obstruction

The fixed-weight selector counterexample in
`candidate 37b334b65d497130` does NOT
obstruct extraction of a convex subbody of mass at least half the
source whose true integer-base centroid has local gamma_4-depth.
This note constructs such a subbody and checks every ambient cap.
It treats this specific n=1,d=4 body only.

## 1. Original body and an actual reflected endpoint pair

Let B be the standard 4-simplex, of volume V, with barycentric
coordinates lambda_0,...,lambda_4. The distinguished coordinate
lambda_1 is the first ordinary coordinate. As in the cited note set

    alpha=17/100, beta=199999/1000000,
    L=B intersect {alpha≤lambda_1≤beta},
    m=|L|/V=(83/100)^4−(800001/1000000)^4,
    Q=m^(−1/4), r=2−Q,
    A=rL, C_+=QL,
    a=|A|/V=(2m^(1/4)−1)^4, h=a^(1/4).

The original mixed fibers at −1,0,1 are A,B,C_+; their total mass
is (2+a)V. The exact bounds proved in the cited note give

    0<a<10^(−8), 0<h<1/100, 0<r<2/101,
    (A+C_+)/2=L⊂B.                                  (1)

Choose v∈B with barycentric coordinates

    lambda_1(v)=37/200,
    lambda_i(v)=163/800 for each i≠1.

These five coordinates are positive and sum to one. Define

    C'=2v−A.

Then C'⊂C_+. Here are explicit inclusion bounds, rather than an
asymptotic assertion. For u∈L, the barycentric coordinates of
`(2v−ru)/Q` are `(2lambda_i(v)−r lambda_i(u))/Q`, since Q=2−r.
For i≠1 their numerators are at least

    163/400−(2/101)(83/100)>0.

For the distinguished coordinate the lower and upper L-slab
conditions follow respectively from

    2(37/200−alpha)−(2/101)(beta−alpha)>0,
    2(beta−37/200)−(2/101)(beta−alpha)>0.

Thus the normalized point belongs to L, proving C'⊂QL. Reflection
preserves volume, so |C'|=aV. The lifted endpoint measure on A at
−1 and C' at +1 is centrally symmetric about (0,v).

## 2. Truncating the middle simplex and computing the true centroid

Remove the small vertex-1 cap from B:

    B_h=B intersect {lambda_1≤1−h}.

Its removed fraction is h^4=a. Its barycentric centroid is
`lambda_1=1−4h/5`, `lambda_i=h/5` for i≠1, by the homothety of
ratio h about vertex 1. Since beta<1−h, L⊂B_h. Therefore

    (A+C')/2⊂(A+C_+)/2=L⊂B_h.

Let D be the convex hull of the three lifted fibers A,B_h,C'.
It is a full-dimensional convex body inside the original body,
and its integer fibers are exactly A,B_h,C'. The displayed
midpoint inclusion proves exactness at the middle base; exactness
at extreme bases follows from extremality. Its mixed mass is

    |D intersect Lambda|_MI=(1+a)V > (2+a)V/2.         (2)

The equal endpoint masses give true integer base centroid zero.
Write c for its continuous centroid. Exact barycentric integration
gives

    lambda_1(c)=1/5−4e,
    lambda_i(c)=1/5+e for i≠1,
    e=(83/400−h/5)a/(1+a).                           (3)

In particular

    a/5≤e≤83a/400<a/4.                               (4)

For the lower bound use
`(83/400−1/500)/(1+10^(−8))>1/5`; the upper bound is immediate.
All coordinates in (3) are positive and lambda_1(c)<1−h, so c
is interior to B_h. We prove

    depth_(D intersect Lambda)((0,c))≥gamma_4,
    gamma_4=Gamma=(4/5)^4.                           (5)

All masses below are divided by V; the target absolute mass is
Gamma(1+a).

## 3. Exact elementary bounds for one-vertex simplex caps

Consider a proper halfspace through c whose trace on the ORIGINAL
B has exactly one strictly positive vertex i. Zero margins at
other vertices are permitted. Its intercept on edge ij is a number
t_j∈(0,1], j≠i. Its cap in B has fraction

    P=product_(j≠i) t_j,
    sum_(j≠i) lambda_j(c)/t_j=1.

Put `b_j=lambda_j(c)/t_j`. These four positive numbers sum to one.
Consequently

    P=product_(j≠i)lambda_j(c) / product_(j≠i)b_j
      ≥4^4 product_(j≠i)lambda_j(c)=P_min,i.          (6)

This is just AM–GM, with no stationarity assumption on the cap.
By (4) every lambda_j(c)≥1/5−a, giving the uniform bound

    P_min,i≥Gamma(1−5a)^4≥Gamma(1−20a).               (7)

There is a useful strict improvement away from balanced intercept
weights. If some b_j is outside [6/25,13/50], then

    product b_j ≤ (1/4)^4(999/1000).

Indeed, fixing one coordinate t gives product at most
`t((1−t)/3)^3`, increasing up to t=1/4 and decreasing afterwards.
At t=6/25 and t=13/50, its ratios to (1/4)^4 are respectively
`3511808/3515625` and `10535824/10546875`, both below 999/1000.
Thus in this case

    P−a≥(1000/999)Gamma(1−20a)−a
         >Gamma(1+a),                                (8)

for 0<a≤10^(−8). The difference is decreasing in a, and at
a=10^(−8) equals `25593999881/62437500000000>0`.
The subtraction by a allows the ENTIRE removed middle cap to be
lost, so (8) already bounds the retained middle mass alone.

## 4. All one-positive-vertex branches

First let the positive vertex be 1. Equations (3)–(4) imply

    P_min,1=4^4(1/5+e)^4≥Gamma(1+a)^4.

After subtracting the removed mass a, this is at least
`Gamma(1+4a)−a`, which exceeds Gamma(1+a) because
`3Gamma−1=143/625>0`. Thus EVERY vertex-1 cap is sufficient,
regardless of its endpoint traces or intercept weights.

Next let i≠1. If an intercept weight is outside the box in Section
3, (8) applies. In the remaining case every b_j∈[6/25,13/50].
In particular

    t_1=lambda_1(c)/b_1≤(1/5)/(6/25)=5/6<1−h.

Every point in the removed vertex-1 cap has lambda_1≥1−h,
and hence lambda_1/t_1>1. It cannot belong to this vertex-i cap.
Therefore NONE of its middle cap volume P was removed.

The same cap strictly contains v. To check this exactly, let

    R_1=(37/200)/(1/5−4e),
    R_o=(163/800)/(1/5+e).

The small bounds in (4) give R_1<1<R_o. Hence

    sum_(j≠i) lambda_j(v)/t_j
       =b_1 R_1+(1−b_1)R_o
       ≤(6/25)*(37/200)/(1/5−10^(−8))
          +(19/25)*(163/800)/(1/5)
       =79699996903/79999996000<1.                    (9)

For any ambient integer tilt, the cap thus contains the symmetry
center (0,v) of the two endpoint fibers. A halfspace containing
the center of a centrally symmetric finite measure captures at
least half that measure: pair each point with its reflection.
The endpoint contribution is therefore at least a.

It remains to bound P_min,i+a. Put t=5e≤83a/80<2a. Since i≠1,

    P_min,i/Gamma=(1−4t)(1+t)^3
                 =1−t−9t^2−11t^3−4t^4.

For 0<a≤10^(−8),

    9t^2+11t^3+4t^4
       ≤36a^2+88a^3+64a^4≤a/80.

Thus P_min,i≥Gamma(1−21a/20), and

    P_min,i+a−Gamma(1+a)
       ≥a[1−(41/20)Gamma]=(501/3125)a>0.             (10)

This handles every one-positive-vertex cap, including zero margins
at any of the other original simplex vertices and all integer tilts.

## 5. Every multi-positive-vertex branch

We use the completely proved scalar lemma in
`candidate 191a0eb2244ea4a9`:
for independent unit exponentials and positive coefficients with
equal positive and negative totals,

    Pr(sum_i A_i E_i ≥ sum_(j=1)^m B_j F_j)≥gamma_m.

That note proves the monotone largest-coefficient merging and all
regularity steps; arbitrary coefficient merging is not being used.

A simplex cap is the event that the affine vertex-margin sum of
normalized independent exponentials is nonnegative. This follows
directly by changing variables E_i=t lambda_i, with Jacobian t^4.
Let k≥2 vertices have positive margins and m have negative margins;
zero margins are omitted. Then k≤4 and 1≤m≤3. Since the margin
vanishes at c and its barycentric coordinates lie between
l=1/5−a and L=1/5+a, the unweighted positive and negative margin
totals A_+,B_- satisfy A_+/B_-≥l/L.

If A_+≥B_-, reduce the positive coefficients to balance them;
this only decreases the cap event and gives probability at least
gamma_m. If A_+<B_-, scale all k positive exponentials by
R=B_-/A_+>1. The scaled k-dimensional density dominates R^(−k)
times the original density, so their total variation distance is
at most 1−R^(−k). The scalar lemma for the balanced event gives
the lower bound

    P≥gamma_m−[1−(A_+/B_-)^k]
      ≥gamma_3−k(1−l/L)≥gamma_3−40a.

Subtracting the entire removed middle mass is still sufficient:

    |B_h intersect H|/V≥gamma_3−41a>Gamma(1+a).       (11)

At a=10^(−8) the difference is exactly
`767161619/62500000000>0`; it is larger for smaller a.
No endpoint contribution is needed in this case.

## 6. Completion for all closed ambient halfspaces

Any containing cap can be moved to have boundary through (0,c),
without increasing its mass. For a nonzero continuous normal this
boundary properly cuts B because all barycentric coordinates of c
are positive. Its vertex margins have at least one strict positive
and one strict negative entry. Sections 3–5 cover all possibilities,
with arbitrary base-normal coefficient throughout.

A purely vertical through-point cap contains the whole middle
fiber B_h. Its mass is at least 1−a>Gamma(1+a), again immediate
from a<10^(−8). Thus (5) follows for every closed halfspace.
Nonvertical boundaries are null on each positive four-dimensional
fiber; vertical boundary fibers have been retained in full.

The point (0,c) is the TRUE centroid of the actual convex subbody
D, not a selected or reweighted original-fiber centroid. Equations
(2) and (5) give exactly the proposed large locally-Grünbaum-deep
extraction for this fixed example. Its depth in the original set
is consequently at least `Gamma(1+a)/(2+a)>Gamma/2`.

This does not establish such an extraction for arbitrary bodies,
other dimensions, or arbitrary retained masses. It decisively
shows why the fixed-weight selector obstruction cannot simply be
promoted to a counterexample against all large convex subbodies:
the small central truncation changes the true centroid and the
near-extremal cap volumes in a controlled, favorable way.
